sections.h2: Fastest way to sell in Sarasota
sections.html:
A cash offer closes soonest in Sarasota, since no lender approval, buyer appraisal or round of repair haggling stands in the way. Listing the house takes longer but shows it to more buyers, and that can lift the price.

Buyers here weigh bay access, flood and wind exposure, and the age of the house. People who want out quickly tend to own an inherited property, a house with deferred repairs, or a rental with a tenant inside. Each situation has its own rules, covered below.

  • Cash purchase: the quickest close, bought as-is, at a negotiated figure.
  • Agent listing: more prep work, a wider market.
  • Private sale: you manage the contract and closing paperwork.

Sarasota grew through recorded plats. Newtown, near downtown, started on April 20, 1914, when its original plat was filed with Manatee County with 96 building lots, and a first addition on August 6, 1914 added 74 more. Lot lines, easements and setbacks on an old plat decide what a buyer may build or add.

If you have an old survey, keep it with the sale papers. If not, a title agent can tell you what the recorded plat shows for your lot.

The office is at 2001 Adams Lane in Sarasota, phone 941.861.8200. It sends a TRIM notice each August, and you can pull a copy of yours through the property search on its website. The site also links Hurricane Evacuation Levels, which buyers sometimes ask about for a specific address.

The office recommends the Clerk's free fraud alert, an email that arrives when a deed or mortgage is recorded in your name.

sections.h2: Tax calendar for a Sarasota seller
sections.html:
Florida property tax calendar as it applies in Sarasota County
EventTiming
Property assessedJanuary 1
Bills mailed; 4 percent discount for payingNovember
Discount drops to 1 percentFebruary
Homestead applications dueMarch 1
Unpaid bills become delinquentApril 1
Tax certificates soldBy June 1

The calendar comes from the state's taxpayer guide. If you sell and then buy again within Florida, part of a Save Our Homes benefit can move to the new house, but only inside the filing window (Save Our Homes guide).

The sale resets the parcel to just value the following January 1. Do not give a buyer a tax estimate built on your current bill.

The state charges 70 cents per hundred dollars of price on a Sarasota County deed, and any loan on the property counts toward that price (s. 201.02). Everyone named on the deed answers to the state, though most contracts assign payment to one side.

The clerk's recording charge is set by s. 28.24 and appears as its own line on the closing statement. Two deeds are exempt from the stamp tax: a spousal homestead deed where the only consideration is a mortgage, and a divorce deed for the marital home (stamp tax page).

• Inherited: an estate of $150,000 or less outside exempt items, or an owner dead more than two years, may use the short summary administration (s. 735.201). Florida levies no estate tax on deaths after 2004.
  • Tenant: nonpayment of rent starts with a three-day notice that leaves out weekends and court holidays (s. 83.56). A breach the tenant can fix gets seven days.
  • Default: once judgment is entered, the clerk auctions the house 20 to 35 days later, and the high bidder puts down a 5 percent deposit (s. 45.031).

Selling ahead of that auction leaves price and timing with you. Money left over after an auction is claimed through the clerk.

Gather the deed, survey, latest tax bill, permit finals and any insurance claim records. Coastal buyers press hard on flood and storm history, so be ready to explain past water or roof damage.

  1. Order a payoff statement from each lender or lienholder.
  2. Confirm homestead status with the Sarasota County Property Appraiser.
  3. Sign up for the Clerk's fraud alerts if the house will sit vacant.
  4. Ask your title agent which documents the Sarasota County recording office wants.

Doing these four things early cuts surprises whether you list or take cash.

Buyers and their insurers will ask where the house sits on the county's hurricane evacuation levels. Look up your address before you list so you can answer directly.

Roof age, window protection and past claims usually follow. Permit records for roof and window work help, as do the product approvals and installer paperwork from those jobs. A permitted, documented roof is easier to insure and to price. A house with gaps in its records can still sell, usually to an investor who plans repairs after closing and builds that cost into the offer.

  • Pull permit finals for roof, windows and electrical.
  • Collect insurance declarations and any claim letters.
  • Write down any past water intrusion and the repair that followed.

A sale touches several offices, and calling the wrong one costs days. Florida counties elect their own property appraiser, tax collector and clerk of the circuit court, and those are separate from city departments.

  • Property appraiser: values, exemptions and the TRIM notice, at 2001 Adams Lane.
  • Tax collector: mails the November bill, takes payment and sells tax certificates on unpaid accounts.
  • Clerk: records the deed, collects stamp tax at recording and runs foreclosure and tax deed sales.
  • City of Sarasota: planning, historic preservation and building matters inside city limits.

Keep each office's name and number in one folder. A title agent can fill gaps, but the owner is usually the first person asked when a record looks wrong.

faqs.q: Where do I find my Sarasota TRIM notice?
faqs.a: On the Sarasota County Property Appraiser's website. Search for your parcel and click the TRIM button. Notices are mailed each August.

faqs.q: Does Sarasota County charge a different deed tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The deed rate is 70 cents per $100 here, the standard statewide rate. Only Miami-Dade differs.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Sarasota house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase as-is. A financed buyer may require repairs, because the lender's appraisal has to support the loan, so condition decides which buyers can close.

faqs.q: Whom should I contact about a Sarasota parcel record?
faqs.a: The county property appraiser, at 941.861.8200 or 2001 Adams Lane.

faqs.q: Do I lose my Save Our Homes benefit when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes for that property, since a sale resets the assessment to just value the next January 1. You may carry part of the benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability, within the filing rules.
